properties.source_path: Papers/002_2026_Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Information Fusion.pdf
properties.venue: Journal of Organizational and End User Computing 38(1)
properties.version_basis: Published article PDF identified by SHA-256; title page read and confirmed.

properties.description: PRISMA-guided systematic review of agentic AI for information fusion: four databases, 1,205 records, 380 included publications, six-dimension taxonomy, qualitative comparative synthesis.
properties.independent_study_claim: a review, not a primary study; its 380 included publications are not counted as annotated studies

properties.description: Conceptual taxonomy and agentic decision-support framework (Figures 1 and 2). Nothing is implemented or evaluated.

properties.decision: architecture selection and research design guidance

properties.description: Literature corpus of 380 publications. The list is public (OSF); the coded corpus is available on request.
properties.label_provenance: coded by an unstated number of reviewers with kappa 0.78 to 0.86 on a 45-study sample

relation_assertions.rationale: Fallback profile for a conceptual contribution. The record is a survey and is not counted as a world model.

capability_assessments.rationale: Survey and review: the framework's state, transition and action statements are claim-stage formalism with no implementation, and cited systems do not transfer capabilities to the review. The core identity rule needs an implemented persistent state advanced by a learned or hybrid transition, which is not met. A text search of all 33 pages found no occurrence of 'world model' or 'digital twin'.

gate_assessments.rationale: For this review G01 is read as the provenance of its own corpus, not model data. Corpus provenance is partial: counts and a coding template exist, but full-text exclusions, search dates in the text and a consistent coder description are missing.

legacy_cells.B: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Information Fusion: Architectures, Coordination, and Decision Intelligence
legacy_cells.C: Dawa Chyophel Lepcha, Aaliya Ali, Bhawna Goyal, Shabbir Syed-Abdul, Loveleen Gaur, Ilan Alon, et al.
legacy_cells.E: journal of organizational and end user computing
legacy_cells.FM: PRISMA-guided systematic review of agentic AI for information fusion; develops a six-dimension taxonomy spanning architecture, learning, coordination, decision coupling, trust, and uncertainty.
legacy_cells.FN: Authors' qualitative synthesis characterizes hybrid cloud–edge and federated architectures with multi-agent reinforcement learning as offering favorable scalability and robustness trade-offs; this is not a new-model experiment.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that formal numerical meta-analysis was precluded by heterogeneity of metrics, evaluation contexts, and experimental designs.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors identify future work on scalable multi-agent coordination, trust calibration, explainability, and foundation-model integration.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors claim that no existing review integrates agentic-AI technical dimensions with organizational and end-user information-systems perspectives.
legacy_cells.FR: This article is a cross-domain literature review, not an implemented patient-state transition model or clinical validation; healthcare examples do not establish healthcare world-model performance.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M9 Safety & governance; M10 Clinician interface & lifecycle
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Carry the paper’s governance and evaluation considerations into a separate safety/lifecycle service; they do not validate a dynamics model.
legacy_cells.FU: Reviewer mapping (KB §20): Prospective evaluation & lifecycle governance
legacy_cells.FX: Title page and Abstract (PDF p. 1); Introduction (pp. 2–4); Methods/PRISMA process (pp. 5–6); fusion foundations and Table 1 (pp. 6–9); agentic taxonomy and Table 2 (pp. 10–12); architectures and Tables 3–4 (pp. 13–21); coordination, learning, trust, uncertainty, and decision coupling (pp. 16–19); healthcare applications (pp. 20–21); comparative synthesis and Table 5 (pp. 22–23); governance/ethics and Challenges/Future Directions (pp. 24–25); Conclusion and data statement (pp. 26–27); references and appendices, including Tables A1/B1 (pp. 28–32); remaining author biographies (p. 33). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Corrected the prefilled title in B because the PDF title page prints the subtitle omitted from metadata. Included as survey/background because healthcare is explicitly reviewed as one application domain, but the article itself does not evaluate a healthcare world model. Extracted tables were legible in the supplied text; no unreadable-table issue noted. Evidence QA: 11/11 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (100%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 13 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: The 380 included studies were not retrieved, so nothing about them is assessed and none is counted as annotated.

Feature assertions are by source scope: own methods (the review's corpus), the authors' framework and recommendations (claim stage) and cited-system descriptions (never inherited). Group-level applicability reasons are reviewer judgment.
World type is unresolved and no readiness facet is assigned (the ontology advises against applying R0 to reviews merely because cited systems are immature).
Schema and quotation occurrence do not prove entailment. Targeted second-model review corrected stage/completeness and attribution; no independent human review or full second re-extraction.

22 November 2026: complete bibliography entries on pp28–30 read; Table1 p9 and AppendixA TableA1 p31/AppendixB TableB1 pp32–33 inspected directly. The appendix is a review extraction template and author-reported coding protocol, not an implemented clinical world model. Earlier full main-text/figure reviews retained; 380 cited studies not retrieved or independently annotated.
notes: Revision r3: feature completeness is scoped to evidence stage. The p. 8 belief exposition is a generic conceptual description; its separately cited Li et al. implementation is not inherited. Survey remains not_world_model.
